## Introduction

The four studies measure different regions, exposures, and assays. They are analyzed separately rather than pooled into a single pollution effect. The reference atlas preserves cell locations and measures 1,122 genes by MERFISH, providing an anatomical setting for selected regional signals. It does not supply exposed single cells. [Read the Introduction](introduction.qmd).

## Methods

The classical workflow includes source and sample checks, count or signal distributions, sample relationships and PCA, differential expression with multiple-testing control, effect-size estimation, and functional enrichment where gene annotations are applicable. Ozone is reprocessed from the original reads. The 3D model uses one bulk gene-specific multiplier within the hypothalamus and keeps the reference cell positions fixed. [Read the Methods](methods.qmd).

```{python}
    ["Hippocampal miRNA · PM2.5", "3 control / 3 low / 3 high", "1 low-dose / 0 high-dose", "Normalized microarray signal", "Strong lower-signal floor"],
    ["Hippocampus · ozone", "24 libraries; 8 groups", " / ".join(str(o['contrasts'][k]['fdr_005']) for k in ["M3_E3_O3_vs_FA", "M3_E4_O3_vs_FA", "M17_E3_O3_vs_FA", "M17_E4_O3_vs_FA"]) + " (four strata)" if ozone_ready else "Raw-read processing in progress", "RNA-seq from FASTQ", "Age × genotype × exposure design"],
]
show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["Study", "Independent samples", "FDR < 0.05", "Evidence", "Interpretive limit"]), n=10)
if ozone_ready:
    display(Markdown(
        f"Ozone counts follow starting-age/genotype order **M3/APOE3, M3/APOE4, M17/APOE3, M17/APOE4**. "
        f"The separate global four-degree-of-freedom exposure LRT identifies **{o['global_LRT']['fdr_005']:,} genes**. "
        "Unequal discovery counts do not establish an age or genotype interaction; the null stratum does not demonstrate absence of response."
    ))
```

These counts are study-specific findings, not a ranking of pollutant toxicity. The sample sizes, tissue composition, protocols, and statistical power differ.

<p class="tag">PRIMARY 3D LINK</p>
### Hypothalamus

Seven animals support the PM2.5 contrast. All eleven primary hits retain their effect direction in leave-one-out fits, but none retains FDR significance in all seven fits. No control was selectively removed.

[Explore the hypothalamus results →](results.qmd)
:::
::: {.study-card}
<p class="tag">REGIONAL RESPONSE</p>
### Cingulate cortex

The PM-versus-PBS contrast is restricted to eight humanized α-synuclein mice. PFF treatment arms are not pooled with this exposure comparison.

[Explore the cortex results →](cortex.qmd)
:::
::: {.study-card}
<p class="tag">A DIFFERENT MOLECULAR LAYER</p>
### Hippocampal miRNA

Two dose-specific contrasts retain the deposited normalized signal scale. Effects are mean signal differences, not RNA-seq counts or confirmed log₂ fold changes.

[Explore the miRNA results →](mirna.qmd)
:::
::: {.study-card}
<p class="tag">AGE AND GENOTYPE</p>
### Hippocampus and ozone

Original paired-end reads are quantified against a fixed mouse reference. Age-, genotype-, and exposure-specific effects are separated in a factorial model.

[Explore the ozone results →](ozone.qmd)

## A measured reference beside an explicit simulation

```{python}
display(Markdown(
    f"**{v['default_gene']}** is the only primary hypothalamic FDR hit measured in this MERFISH panel. "
    f"Its central regional multiplier is **{v['default_multiplier']:.3f}×**. The viewer contains "
    f"**{v['measured_genes']:,} measured genes**, with reliable bulk effect estimates for "
    f"**{v['genes_with_estimable_bulk_effect']:,}** of them; nonsignificant genes are labeled exploratory."
))
```

[![Measured spatial reference and modeled PM2.5 scenario for Tll1, with the same hypothalamic cell positions.](assets/figures/spatial_viewer/reference_vs_simulation.png){.site-overview-image}](viewer.qmd)

::: {.model-note}
**A modeled scenario, not exposed spatial data.** The atlas donor is not an experimental control for the seven bulk animals. A uniform regional multiplier does not identify which cell types respond, and it does not model cell loss, movement, or anatomical change.
:::
